source_problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨1,\,0,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)$ for $-\pi \le x\le 0$ and $-x\le y\le 0.$
interpreted_problem: Evaluate exactly the FORMAL repeated integral $\int_{-\pi}^{0}\int_{-x}^{0}(\sin(x+y)+y)\,dy\,dx$, with the printed lower and upper limits in that order and the conventional signed-integral rule for reversed limits. This distinct request does not assert that this integral is the flux over the surface in the original source. The original inequalities $-\pi\le x\le0$, $-x\le y\le0$ instead define the singleton projection $(0,0)$, of area zero. Choose the exact value of this formal repeated integral from the supplied original choices.
